mainEntity.name: How much does a Range Rover D350 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt or reconditioned engine replacement for a Range Rover D350 typically ranges from £7,500 to £11,000 for supply only, depending on the specialist and the extent of upgrades included. Used engines start around £3,500 but carry higher risk, while rebuilt units include upgraded components and a 12-month warranty.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of a failing DT306 engine in a Range Rover D350?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning signs in the Range Rover D350 are a distinct knocking noise from the bottom end on cold starts, illuminated oil pressure warning lights, or a noticeable loss of power and excessive smoke. You should also watch for metallic debris in the oil filter during servicing.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Range Rover D350?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A typical Range Rover D350 holds a UK market value of £55,000-£120,000+, making a £7,500-£11,000 rebuilt engine a financially sound investment that preserves the vehicle's performance, refinement, and strong resale value for years to come.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Range Rover D350 engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional supply and fit service for a Range Rover D350 typically takes 3 to 5 days, depending on the specialist's workload and whether any ancillary components like the 48V mild-hybrid system are being calibrated simultaneously. Sourcing a quality rebuilt unit may add a few days.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the Range Rover D350 and the P400 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Range Rover D350 uses a 3.0-litre inline-6 mild-hybrid diesel engine (DT306/306DT) producing 350 PS and 700 Nm of torque, prioritising low-end pulling power and fuel efficiency for long-distance touring. In contrast, the P400 uses a 3.0-litre inline-6 mild-hybrid petrol engine producing 400 PS, focused on higher-revving performance and smoother refinement.

historyTimeline.h2: Range Rover D350 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the all-new L460 Range Rover launched, the D350 badge represented the core diesel offering - a refined, high-output 3.0-litre inline-six mild-hybrid diesel delivering effortless torque and exceptional refinement for the flagship SUV.

milestones.description: Introduction of the DT306 / 306DT 3.0L inline-6 mild-hybrid diesel engine (350 PS / 345 hp, 700 Nm) in the L460 Range Rover D350, paired with an 8-speed ZF automatic and permanent four-wheel drive.

Present - Continued production with minor software calibrations for the 48V mild-hybrid system to improve emissions compliance and throttle response; the core 3.0L Ingenium diesel architecture remains unchanged.

commonProblems.h2: Range Rover D350 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The 3.0-litre Ingenium inline-six diesel (DT306/306DT) in the Range Rover D350 is a refined and capable powerplant, but the broader 306DT family has a known history of bottom-end wear if maintenance intervals are extended. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Crankshaft Bearing & Oil Pump Wear - Why the Range Rover D350 DT306 Requires Attention
problems.typicalFailureMileage: 80,000-140,000 miles (Note: L460 models are newer, but this is the established pattern for the 306DT architecture).
problems.rootCause: Tin-aluminium coating fatigue on crankshaft bearings, compounded by oil pump pressure drops or extended oil change intervals, can lead to catastrophic bottom-end failure and engine seizure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace oil pump, inspect bearings via borescope, and flush system with premium synthetic oil.
repairOptions.longevity: Highly effective preventative measure if caught before any knocking or pressure loss occurs.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded bottom-end components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The only reliable long-term solution if the engine has already suffered bearing knock or seizure.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Range Rover D350 of relevant age (2022-present) currently holds a UK market value of approximately £55,000-£120,000+ [THIRD-PARTY - Auto Trader / Cazoo market observations]. At this premium value band, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine replacement is a small fraction of the vehicle's worth and easily justifies the investment to preserve performance, refinement, and strong resale value.
problems.recommendation: Strict adherence to 10,000-mile oil change intervals is the single most effective preventative measure for the Range Rover D350. If you hear a cold-start knock or experience an oil pressure warning, cease driving immediately. A full rebuilt replacement is the only viable path to protect your investment once internal damage has occurred.
